content.content:
1	# Scraper
2	
3	Tools for scraping show data from [edfringe.com](https://www.edfringe.com).
4	
5	> For the API itself — endpoints, auth, the full `EventDetail` field surface, and
6	> the non-obvious bits (pricing lives behind a separate per-performance query;
7	> `ticketStatus` vs the `soldOut` flag) — see **[SCRAPING.md](SCRAPING.md)**.
8	
9	## How edfringe.com serves listings
10	
11	The "What's On" listing (`/tickets/whats-on?page=N`) is a **Next.js single-page
12	app**. The server returns the same ~20 KB JavaScript shell for every page and
13	the shows are loaded **client-side from a GraphQL API**. So fetching the HTML
14	yields empty pages — there is no show data in the markup to extract.
15	
16	The shows come from:
17	
18	```
19	POST https://edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com/graphql
20	```
21	
22	authenticated with a bearer token from `POST .../token` using the site's public
23	anonymous credentials. The `EventsSearch` operation returns structured JSON
24	(title, genre, dates, venues, spaces, performances, prices, images, …), 50
25	shows per page, ~3,800 shows over ~77 pages.
26	
27	## fetch_shows.py — download all shows from the API
28	
29	```
30	python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py
31	```
32	
33	- Authenticates, then pages through every show via the GraphQL API.
34	- Output (default `data/raw_pages/`):
35	  - `page_NN.json` — the raw `events` payload per page (kept for re-processing).
36	  - `shows.json` — all show results flattened into a single array.
37	- A random 4–9 s delay is inserted between requests.
38	- **Resumable**: existing `page_NN.json` files are skipped; use `--force` to
39	  re-fetch. A fixed `--seed` keeps the server ordering stable across pages so
40	  paging never skips or duplicates shows.
41	
42	Options:
43	
44	```
45	python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py \
46	    --per 50 --seed 123 --min-delay 4 --max-delay 9 \
47	    --out-dir data/raw_pages [--max-pages N] [--force]
48	```
49	
50	The raw output is **git-ignored** (see `.gitignore`) — it is a regenerable
51	cache, not source.
52	
53	## normalize.py — turn the raw scrape into website data
54	
55	```
56	python3 scraper/normalize.py
57	```
58	
59	Reads the raw scrape and emits three layers (these **are** committed, since the
60	site serves them):
61	
62	| file | purpose | sent to browser |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| `data/normalized/shows.json` | master: one record per show with all performances (including each show's full `description`); source for regenerating everything below | no |
65	| `data/normalized/shows.min.json` | the compact catalogue the planner downloads: the master packed losslessly against the `venues.json` lookups | yes (planner) |
66	| `data/normalized/descriptions.min.json` | `{v, d: {slug → full description}}`, kept out of the catalogue above so that file stays small enough to block on. Fetched lazily by the planner and cached for a week; the hover card and search fall back to the catalogue's 160-char `blurb` until it lands | yes (planner, lazily) |
67	| `data/venues.json` | shared lookup sent once: `{ venues, rooms, genres, subgenres, ticketStatuses }` — venue map (code → name, address, postcode, lat, lng) plus the global lookup lists | yes (once) |
68	| `data/days/2026-08-DD.json` | per-day shows with the minimum a card needs (venue, genre, room, subgenres and ticket status referenced by index) | yes (today's) |
69	| `data/days/index.json` | available days + per-day counts | yes |
70	
71	Normalization rules:
72	- **Location** = venue code (the "venue number") + the show's room (space); venue
73	  name/address/coords live only in `venues.json`.
74	- **Shared lookups live once, in `venues.json`.** It is a
75	  `{ "venues": {...}, "rooms": [...], "genres": [...] }` container: `rooms` and
76	  `genres` are the global de-duplicated string lists (~420 rooms, 10 genres).
77	  The browser already fetches this file once, so the lists cost one small
78	  download rather than being repeated in every day file.
79	- **Day files are compact.** Each `2026-08-DD.json` is a plain array of shows; a
80	  show's `genre`, `room`, `subs` (subgenres) and `ts` (ticket status) are indices
81	  into the matching global lists (`room`/`ts` are -1 when unknown). Binary flags
82	  (`free`, `soldOut`) are 1/0, and the `blurb` — kept in the master but never
83	  rendered by the site — is dropped. This more than halves the day payload.
84	- **Ticket status** (`ts` → `ticketStatuses`) is the reliable "can I get a
85	  ticket" signal, not the `soldOut` flag (a show can be `soldOut:false` yet have
86	  no online allocation). Because it changes through the day, the
87	  `refresh-tickets` scheduled task (`refresh_ticket_status.py`) updates just
88	  today's `ts` values each hour during the festival — a light paged pass, no

# Scraper

Tools for scraping show data from [edfringe.com](https://www.edfringe.com).

> For the API itself — endpoints, auth, the full `EventDetail` field surface, and
> the non-obvious bits (pricing lives behind a separate per-performance query;
> `ticketStatus` vs the `soldOut` flag) — see **[SCRAPING.md](SCRAPING.md)**.

## How edfringe.com serves listings

The "What's On" listing (`/tickets/whats-on?page=N`) is a **Next.js single-page
app**. The server returns the same ~20 KB JavaScript shell for every page and
the shows are loaded **client-side from a GraphQL API**. So fetching the HTML
yields empty pages — there is no show data in the markup to extract.

The shows come from:

```
POST https://edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com/graphql
```

authenticated with a bearer token from `POST .../token` using the site's public
anonymous credentials. The `EventsSearch` operation returns structured JSON
(title, genre, dates, venues, spaces, performances, prices, images, …), 50
shows per page, ~3,800 shows over ~77 pages.

## fetch_shows.py — download all shows from the API

```
python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py
```

- Authenticates, then pages through every show via the GraphQL API.
- Output (default `data/raw_pages/`):
  - `page_NN.json` — the raw `events` payload per page (kept for re-processing).
  - `shows.json` — all show results flattened into a single array.
- A random 4–9 s delay is inserted between requests.
- **Resumable**: existing `page_NN.json` files are skipped; use `--force` to
  re-fetch. A fixed `--seed` keeps the server ordering stable across pages so
  paging never skips or duplicates shows.

Options:

```
python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py \
    --per 50 --seed 123 --min-delay 4 --max-delay 9 \
    --out-dir data/raw_pages [--max-pages N] [--force]
```

The raw output is **git-ignored** (see `.gitignore`) — it is a regenerable
cache, not source.

## normalize.py — turn the raw scrape into website data

```
python3 scraper/normalize.py
```

Reads the raw scrape and emits three layers (these **are** committed, since the
site serves them):

| file | purpose | sent to browser |
|---|---|---|
| `data/normalized/shows.json` | master: one record per show with all performances (including each show's full `description`); source for regenerating everything below | no |
| `data/normalized/shows.min.json` | the compact catalogue the planner downloads: the master packed losslessly against the `venues.json` lookups | yes (planner) |
| `data/normalized/descriptions.min.json` | `{v, d: {slug → full description}}`, kept out of the catalogue above so that file stays small enough to block on. Fetched lazily by the planner and cached for a week; the hover card and search fall back to the catalogue's 160-char `blurb` until it lands | yes (planner, lazily) |
| `data/venues.json` | shared lookup sent once: `{ venues, rooms, genres, subgenres, ticketStatuses }` — venue map (code → name, address, postcode, lat, lng) plus the global lookup lists | yes (once) |
| `data/days/2026-08-DD.json` | per-day shows with the minimum a card needs (venue, genre, room, subgenres and ticket status referenced by index) | yes (today's) |
| `data/days/index.json` | available days + per-day counts | yes |

Normalization rules:
- **Location** = venue code (the "venue number") + the show's room (space); venue
  name/address/coords live only in `venues.json`.
- **Shared lookups live once, in `venues.json`.** It is a
  `{ "venues": {...}, "rooms": [...], "genres": [...] }` container: `rooms` and
  `genres` are the global de-duplicated string lists (~420 rooms, 10 genres).
  The browser already fetches this file once, so the lists cost one small
  download rather than being repeated in every day file.
- **Day files are compact.** Each `2026-08-DD.json` is a plain array of shows; a
  show's `genre`, `room`, `subs` (subgenres) and `ts` (ticket status) are indices
  into the matching global lists (`room`/`ts` are -1 when unknown). Binary flags
  (`free`, `soldOut`) are 1/0, and the `blurb` — kept in the master but never
  rendered by the site — is dropped. This more than halves the day payload.
- **Ticket status** (`ts` → `ticketStatuses`) is the reliable "can I get a
  ticket" signal, not the `soldOut` flag (a show can be `soldOut:false` yet have
  no online allocation). Because it changes through the day, the
  `refresh-tickets` scheduled task (`refresh_ticket_status.py`) updates just
  today's `ts` values each hour during the festival — a light paged pass, no
  per-show queries.
- **Images**: the master keeps both `image` (the API's "Large" variant) and
  `smallImage` (the "Small" variant), each selected by `imageType` rather than
  list order. Every listing image lives under
  `http://registration.edfringe.com/resource/image/<guid>`, so the master stores
  only the bare `<guid>` and the client re-attaches the host (over https); this
  trims ~50 bytes off each image field in `shows.json`. Not in the day files yet.
- **Price** = a `free` flag (the listing API exposes no amount).
- **Coordinates** are geocoded from each venue's UK postcode via
  [postcodes.io](https://postcodes.io) and cached in `venues.json`, so a refresh
  only geocodes new venues. Use `--no-geocode` to skip.
- **Genre** is mapped to the site's ten categories.
- **Subgenres** are the finer descriptors the festival tags each show with
  (e.g. Stand-up, Improv, New writing, Drama) — carried through from the API's
  `subGenre`/`subgenres` fields as a list of display labels, for display only
  (not a filter). About 2% of shows carry none.

`python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest` runs a built-in transform test (no
network or scraped data needed).

## Refreshing data (daily)

A full re-scrape isn't needed to stay current. The **daily** path fetches only
shows added/updated in the last seven days and merges them in:

```
python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py --recently-added LAST_SEVEN_DAYS
python3 scraper/normalize.py --merge
```

`--merge` upserts the new shows into the existing master (by id) and regenerates
the venue and per-day files. This runs automatically once a day as the
**`refresh-shows`** scheduled task (see *How the scheduled refreshes run* below);
the full rebuild stays a manual workflow, **`Scrape edfringe shows (full)`**
(`.github/workflows/scrape.yml`). Both commit the updated data back to the repo.

## How the scheduled refreshes run

Neither refresh has a workflow of its own. The repo's only cron is the Claudinite
scheduler (`.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`), which runs hourly and
evaluates every declared task's precondition; the two data refreshes are declared
as tasks under this repo's local pack, each with the shell it runs beside it:

| Task | Runs | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `refresh-shows` | daily | the `--recently-added LAST_SEVEN_DAYS` top-up above |
| `refresh-tickets` | hourly, but only in August between 08:00 and 23:59 Edinburgh time | `refresh_ticket_status.py` for today |

`refresh-tickets` is evaluated every hour year-round and its precondition decides
whether to act — that August/hours window is the whole of what sixteen
hand-written cron lines used to express. Both tasks run as plain subprocesses (no
agent); a failure opens one tracking issue rather than passing silently.

## Running it

`equhost.com` must be reachable from wherever you run this. Claude Code web
sessions sit behind an egress proxy that may block it; in that case run the
script locally, or use the **`Scrape edfringe listing pages`** GitHub Action
(`.github/workflows/scrape.yml`), which runs on a GitHub-hosted runner with open
network access and uploads the result as an artifact.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Scrape all Edinburgh Fringe shows from the edfringe.com data API.
3	
4	The edfringe.com "What's On" listing is a Next.js app that loads shows
5	client-side from a GraphQL API; the HTML pages are an empty shell. This script
6	talks to that API directly, which is both far cleaner (structured JSON) and
7	much kinder to the site than rendering HTML.
8	
9	Flow:
10	  1. POST /token with the site's public anonymous credentials -> bearer token.
11	  2. POST /graphql `EventsSearch` for each page (50 shows per page), paging
12	     until every show has been fetched. `total` from the first response tells
13	     us how many pages there are (~77).
14	
15	Output (default data/raw_pages/):
16	  * page_NN.json   - the raw `events` payload for each page (for later re-use)
17	  * shows.json     - all show results flattened into a single array
18	
19	Behaviour mirrors the original downloader: a random delay between requests,
20	resumable (existing page files are skipped), atomic writes.
21	
22	Usage:
23	    python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py                  # fetch every page
24	    python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py --min-delay 4 --max-delay 9
25	    python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py --force          # re-fetch all pages
26	    python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py --per 50 --season EDFRINGE-2026
27	"""
28	
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	import argparse
32	import json
33	import math
34	import random
35	import sys
36	import time
37	from pathlib import Path
38	from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
39	from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
40	
41	API_BASE = "https://edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com"
42	TOKEN_URL = f"{API_BASE}/token"
43	GRAPHQL_URL = f"{API_BASE}/graphql"
44	
45	# Public anonymous credentials embedded in the site's JavaScript. They only
46	# grant read access to the same public listing the website shows to everyone.
47	DEFAULT_USERNAME = "anonymous"
48	DEFAULT_PASSWORD = "2add50c2-ac54-4c1e-b5bc-f8d9ca66a067"
49	
50	DEFAULT_OUT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "raw_pages"
51	DEFAULT_PER = 50
52	# Fixed seed so the server's ordering is stable across paged requests; without
53	# it a randomised sort could duplicate/skip shows between pages.
54	DEFAULT_SEED = "123"
55	
56	# The exact EventsSearch operation the website sends (captured from the app).
57	VENUES_QUERY = """
58	    query VenueTypeAhead($geoLocation: GeoSearchDtoInput, $sort: SortBy) {
59	  venues(input: {page: 0, per: 1000, geo: $geoLocation, sortBy: $sort}) {
60	    total
61	    per
62	    page
63	    results {
64	      ...VenueTypeAhead
65	    }
66	  }
67	}
68	
69	    fragment VenueTypeAhead on VenueDetail {
70	  id
71	  title
72	  description
73	  venueCode
74	  address1
75	  address2
76	  postCode
77	  distance
78	}
79	    """
80	
81	GENRES_QUERY = """
82	    query Genres {
83	  genres {
84	    label
85	    iconName
86	    value
87	  }
88	}
89	    """
90	
91	EVENTS_SEARCH_QUERY = """
92	    query EventsSearch($criteria: SearchCriteriaInput!) {
93	  events(input: $criteria) {
94	    total
95	    page
96	    per
97	    results {
98	      ...EventSearchResult
99	    }
100	  }
101	}
102	
103	    fragment EventSearchResult on EventDetail {
104	  id
105	  title
106	  genre
107	  subGenre
108	  subgenres
109	  startingDate
110	  endingDate
111	  datesDisplay
112	  hasVariousStartingTime
113	  duration
114	  boxOfficeRef
115	  accessibility
116	  accessibilityNotes
117	  distance
118	  cmsRef
119	  slug
120	  priceType
121	  freeTicketed
122	  canceleld
123	  performances {
124	    ...PerformanceMaster
125	  }
126	  presentedBy
127	  description
128	  ageRestriction
129	  venues {
130	    title
131	    slug
132	  }
133	  spaces {
134	    id
135	    title
136	    venueName
137	    venueCode
138	  }
139	  images {
140	    url
141	    imageType
142	    boxOfficeId
143	    cmsId
144	  }
145	  attributes {
146	    id
147	    key
148	    attributeTypes
149	    value
150	    eventCode
151	  }
152	}
153	
154	    fragment PerformanceMaster on PerformanceMaster {
155	  id
156	  title
157	  dateTime
158	  estimatedEndDateTime
159	  status
160	  duration
161	  notes
162	  cancelled
163	  soldOut
164	  boxOfficeId
165	  boxOfficeRef
166	  ticketsAvailable
167	  accessibility
168	  ticketStatus
169	  badges {
170	    label
171	    colour
172	  }
173	  concessions {
174	    code
175	    concessionRef
176	    description
177	    scheme_ref
178	    title
179	  }
180	}
181	    """
182	
183	USER_AGENT = (
184	    "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 "
185	    "(KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
186	)
187	REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 30
188	MAX_RETRIES = 3
189	
190	# Process start; used to prefix progress lines with elapsed time so a long,
191	# mostly-sleeping crawl still shows visible movement in the CI log.
192	START = time.monotonic()
193	
194	
195	def elapsed() -> str:
196	    """Elapsed wall time since start as m:ss, e.g. '3:07'."""
197	    secs = int(time.monotonic() - START)
198	    return f"{secs // 60}:{secs % 60:02d}"
199	
200	
201	def post_json(url: str, payload: dict, token: str | None = None) -> dict:
202	    """POST JSON, retrying transient failures, returning the decoded response."""
203	    body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
204	    headers = {
205	        "Content-Type": "application/json",
206	        "Accept": "application/json",
207	        "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
208	        "Origin": "https://www.edfringe.com",
209	    }
210	    if token:
211	        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
212	
213	    last_err: Exception | None = None
214	    for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1):
215	        try:
216	            req = Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method="POST")
217	            with urlopen(req, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT) as resp:
218	                return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
219	        except HTTPError as exc:
220	            # Auth expiry or bad request won't fix themselves on retry.
221	            if exc.code in (400, 401, 403):
222	                raise
223	            last_err = exc
224	        except (URLError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
225	            last_err = exc
226	        if attempt < MAX_RETRIES:
227	            backoff = 2 ** attempt
228	            print(f"    retry {attempt}/{MAX_RETRIES - 1} after {backoff}s "
229	                  f"({last_err})", file=sys.stderr)
230	            time.sleep(backoff)
231	    raise RuntimeError(f"POST {url} failed: {last_err}")
232	
233	
234	def get_token(username: str, password: str) -> str:
235	    data = post_json(TOKEN_URL, {"username": username, "password": password})
236	    token = data.get("token")
237	    if not token:
238	        raise RuntimeError(f"no token in response: {data}")
239	    return token
240	
241	
242	def fetch_events_page(token: str, page: int, per: int, seed: str,
243	                      recently_added: str = "ANY") -> dict:
244	    payload = {
245	        "query": EVENTS_SEARCH_QUERY,
246	        "variables": {"criteria": {
247	            "page": page,
248	            "per": per,
249	            "sortBy": "TITLE",
250	            "sortBySeed": seed,
251	            "recentlyAdded": recently_added,
252	        }},
253	        "operationName": "EventsSearch",
254	    }
255	    data = post_json(GRAPHQL_URL, payload, token=token)
256	    if "errors" in data:
257	        raise RuntimeError(f"GraphQL errors on page {page}: {data['errors']}")
258	    return data["data"]["events"]
259	
260	
261	def fetch_venues(token: str) -> dict:
262	    payload = {
263	        "query": VENUES_QUERY,
264	        "variables": {"sort": "TITLE"},
265	        "operationName": "VenueTypeAhead",
266	    }
267	    data = post_json(GRAPHQL_URL, payload, token=token)
268	    if "errors" in data:
269	        raise RuntimeError(f"GraphQL errors fetching venues: {data['errors']}")
270	    return data["data"]["venues"]
271	
272	
273	def fetch_genres(token: str) -> list:
274	    payload = {"query": GENRES_QUERY, "operationName": "Genres"}
275	    data = post_json(GRAPHQL_URL, payload, token=token)
276	    if "errors" in data:
277	        raise RuntimeError(f"GraphQL errors fetching genres: {data['errors']}")
278	    return data["data"]["genres"]
279	
280	
281	def main() -> int:
282	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
283	                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
284	    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT_DIR,
285	                        help=f"output directory (default {DEFAULT_OUT_DIR})")
286	    parser.add_argument("--per", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PER,
287	                        help=f"shows per page (default {DEFAULT_PER})")
288	    parser.add_argument("--seed", default=DEFAULT_SEED,
289	                        help="sortBySeed for stable paging (default %(default)s)")
290	    parser.add_argument("--season", default="EDFRINGE-2026",
291	                        help="season code, informational (default %(default)s)")
292	    parser.add_argument("--username", default=DEFAULT_USERNAME)
293	    parser.add_argument("--password", default=DEFAULT_PASSWORD)
294	    parser.add_argument("--min-delay", type=float, default=4.0,
295	                        help="minimum delay between requests, seconds (default 4)")
296	    parser.add_argument("--max-delay", type=float, default=9.0,
297	                        help="maximum delay between requests, seconds (default 9)")
298	    parser.add_argument("--max-pages", type=int, default=None,
299	                        help="cap the number of pages (default: all)")
300	    parser.add_argument("--recently-added", default="ANY",
301	                        choices=["ANY", "LAST_SEVEN_DAYS", "LAST_TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS"],
302	                        help="filter to recently added shows (default ANY; use "
303	                             "LAST_SEVEN_DAYS for a daily refresh)")
304	    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
305	                        help="re-fetch pages even if they already exist")
306	    args = parser.parse_args()
307	
308	    # In CI, stdout is a pipe (not a TTY), so Python fully buffers it and none
309	    # of the progress below appears until the process exits — a multi-minute
310	    # crawl looks frozen. Force line buffering so each line is flushed as it is
311	    # printed. (`python -u` or PYTHONUNBUFFERED would also work; doing it here
312	    # keeps the script self-contained regardless of how it is launched.)
313	    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
314	        try:
315	            stream.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)
316	        except (AttributeError, ValueError):
317	            pass
318	
319	    if args.min_delay > args.max_delay:
320	        parser.error("--min-delay must not exceed --max-delay")
321	
322	    out_dir: Path = args.out_dir
323	    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
324	
325	    print(f"[{elapsed()}] Authenticating...")
326	    token = get_token(args.username, args.password)
327	
328	    # Reference data: genres (for mapping) and venues (for addresses). Small,
329	    # so always refresh them alongside the events.
330	    print(f"[{elapsed()}] Fetching genres and venues...")
331	    genres = fetch_genres(token)
332	    (out_dir / "genres_raw.json").write_text(
333	        json.dumps(genres, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
334	    venues = fetch_venues(token)
335	    (out_dir / "venues_raw.json").write_text(
336	        json.dumps(venues, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
337	    print(f"[{elapsed()}]   {len(genres)} genres, {venues.get('total', '?')} venues")
338	
339	    # First page tells us the total so we know how many pages to fetch.
340	    print(f"[{elapsed()}] Fetching page 1 (recentlyAdded={args.recently_added}) "
341	          "to determine total...")
342	    first = fetch_events_page(token, 1, args.per, args.seed, args.recently_added)
343	    total = first["total"]
344	    total_pages = max(1, math.ceil(total / args.per))
345	    if args.max_pages:
346	        total_pages = min(total_pages, args.max_pages)
347	    width = max(2, len(str(total_pages)))
348	    # Rough finish estimate from the average inter-request delay (each page but
349	    # the last is followed by one sleep).
350	    est_secs = (total_pages - 1) * (args.min_delay + args.max_delay) / 2
351	    print(f"[{elapsed()}] {total} shows across {total_pages} pages (per={args.per}); "
352	          f"~{int(est_secs // 60)}m of throttled fetching to go")
353	
354	    all_shows: list[dict] = []
355	
356	    def save_page(page: int, events: dict) -> None:
357	        dest = out_dir / f"page_{page:0{width}d}.json"
358	        tmp = dest.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
359	        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(events, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
360	        tmp.replace(dest)
361	
362	    fetched = skipped = failed = 0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scrape all Edinburgh Fringe shows from the edfringe.com data API.

The edfringe.com "What's On" listing is a Next.js app that loads shows
client-side from a GraphQL API; the HTML pages are an empty shell. This script
talks to that API directly, which is both far cleaner (structured JSON) and
much kinder to the site than rendering HTML.

Flow:
  1. POST /token with the site's public anonymous credentials -> bearer token.
  2. POST /graphql `EventsSearch` for each page (50 shows per page), paging
     until every show has been fetched. `total` from the first response tells
     us how many pages there are (~77).

Output (default data/raw_pages/):
  * page_NN.json   - the raw `events` payload for each page (for later re-use)
  * shows.json     - all show results flattened into a single array

Behaviour mirrors the original downloader: a random delay between requests,
resumable (existing page files are skipped), atomic writes.

Usage:
    python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py                  # fetch every page
    python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py --min-delay 4 --max-delay 9
    python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py --force          # re-fetch all pages
    python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py --per 50 --season EDFRINGE-2026
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import random
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError

API_BASE = "https://edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com"
TOKEN_URL = f"{API_BASE}/token"
GRAPHQL_URL = f"{API_BASE}/graphql"

# Public anonymous credentials embedded in the site's JavaScript. They only
# grant read access to the same public listing the website shows to everyone.
DEFAULT_USERNAME = "anonymous"
DEFAULT_PASSWORD = "2add50c2-ac54-4c1e-b5bc-f8d9ca66a067"

DEFAULT_OUT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "raw_pages"
DEFAULT_PER = 50
# Fixed seed so the server's ordering is stable across paged requests; without
# it a randomised sort could duplicate/skip shows between pages.
DEFAULT_SEED = "123"

# The exact EventsSearch operation the website sends (captured from the app).
VENUES_QUERY = """
    query VenueTypeAhead($geoLocation: GeoSearchDtoInput, $sort: SortBy) {
  venues(input: {page: 0, per: 1000, geo: $geoLocation, sortBy: $sort}) {
    total
    per
    page
    results {
      ...VenueTypeAhead
    }
  }
}

    fragment VenueTypeAhead on VenueDetail {
  id
  title
  description
  venueCode
  address1
  address2
  postCode
  distance
}
    """

GENRES_QUERY = """
    query Genres {
  genres {
    label
    iconName
    value
  }
}
    """

EVENTS_SEARCH_QUERY = """
    query EventsSearch($criteria: SearchCriteriaInput!) {
  events(input: $criteria) {
    total
    page
    per
    results {
      ...EventSearchResult
    }
  }
}

    fragment EventSearchResult on EventDetail {
  id
  title
  genre
  subGenre
  subgenres
  startingDate
  endingDate
  datesDisplay
  hasVariousStartingTime
  duration
  boxOfficeRef
  accessibility
  accessibilityNotes
  distance
  cmsRef
  slug
  priceType
  freeTicketed
  canceleld
  performances {
    ...PerformanceMaster
  }
  presentedBy
  description
  ageRestriction
  venues {
    title
    slug
  }
  spaces {
    id
    title
    venueName
    venueCode
  }
  images {
    url
    imageType
    boxOfficeId
    cmsId
  }
  attributes {
    id
    key
    attributeTypes
    value
    eventCode
  }
}

    fragment PerformanceMaster on PerformanceMaster {
  id
  title
  dateTime
  estimatedEndDateTime
  status
  duration
  notes
  cancelled
  soldOut
  boxOfficeId
  boxOfficeRef
  ticketsAvailable
  accessibility
  ticketStatus
  badges {
    label
    colour
  }
  concessions {
    code
    concessionRef
    description
    scheme_ref
    title
  }
}
    """

USER_AGENT = (
    "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 "
    "(KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
)
REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 30
MAX_RETRIES = 3

# Process start; used to prefix progress lines with elapsed time so a long,
# mostly-sleeping crawl still shows visible movement in the CI log.
START = time.monotonic()


def elapsed() -> str:
    """Elapsed wall time since start as m:ss, e.g. '3:07'."""
    secs = int(time.monotonic() - START)
    return f"{secs // 60}:{secs % 60:02d}"


def post_json(url: str, payload: dict, token: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """POST JSON, retrying transient failures, returning the decoded response."""
    body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Accept": "application/json",
        "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
        "Origin": "https://www.edfringe.com",
    }
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"

    last_err: Exception | None = None
    for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1):
        try:
            req = Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method="POST")
            with urlopen(req, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT) as resp:
                return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
        except HTTPError as exc:
            # Auth expiry or bad request won't fix themselves on retry.
            if exc.code in (400, 401, 403):
                raise
            last_err = exc
        except (URLError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            last_err = exc
        if attempt < MAX_RETRIES:
            backoff = 2 ** attempt
            print(f"    retry {attempt}/{MAX_RETRIES - 1} after {backoff}s "
                  f"({last_err})", file=sys.stderr)
            time.sleep(backoff)
    raise RuntimeError(f"POST {url} failed: {last_err}")


def get_token(username: str, password: str) -> str:
    data = post_json(TOKEN_URL, {"username": username, "password": password})
    token = data.get("token")
    if not token:
        raise RuntimeError(f"no token in response: {data}")
    return token


def fetch_events_page(token: str, page: int, per: int, seed: str,
                      recently_added: str = "ANY") -> dict:
    payload = {
        "query": EVENTS_SEARCH_QUERY,
        "variables": {"criteria": {
            "page": page,
            "per": per,
            "sortBy": "TITLE",
            "sortBySeed": seed,
            "recentlyAdded": recently_added,
        }},
        "operationName": "EventsSearch",
    }
    data = post_json(GRAPHQL_URL, payload, token=token)
    if "errors" in data:
        raise RuntimeError(f"GraphQL errors on page {page}: {data['errors']}")
    return data["data"]["events"]


def fetch_venues(token: str) -> dict:
    payload = {
        "query": VENUES_QUERY,
        "variables": {"sort": "TITLE"},
        "operationName": "VenueTypeAhead",
    }
    data = post_json(GRAPHQL_URL, payload, token=token)
    if "errors" in data:
        raise RuntimeError(f"GraphQL errors fetching venues: {data['errors']}")
    return data["data"]["venues"]


def fetch_genres(token: str) -> list:
    payload = {"query": GENRES_QUERY, "operationName": "Genres"}
    data = post_json(GRAPHQL_URL, payload, token=token)
    if "errors" in data:
        raise RuntimeError(f"GraphQL errors fetching genres: {data['errors']}")
    return data["data"]["genres"]


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT_DIR,
                        help=f"output directory (default {DEFAULT_OUT_DIR})")
    parser.add_argument("--per", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PER,
                        help=f"shows per page (default {DEFAULT_PER})")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", default=DEFAULT_SEED,
                        help="sortBySeed for stable paging (default %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument("--season", default="EDFRINGE-2026",
                        help="season code, informational (default %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument("--username", default=DEFAULT_USERNAME)
    parser.add_argument("--password", default=DEFAULT_PASSWORD)
    parser.add_argument("--min-delay", type=float, default=4.0,
                        help="minimum delay between requests, seconds (default 4)")
    parser.add_argument("--max-delay", type=float, default=9.0,
                        help="maximum delay between requests, seconds (default 9)")
    parser.add_argument("--max-pages", type=int, default=None,
                        help="cap the number of pages (default: all)")
    parser.add_argument("--recently-added", default="ANY",
                        choices=["ANY", "LAST_SEVEN_DAYS", "LAST_TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS"],
                        help="filter to recently added shows (default ANY; use "
                             "LAST_SEVEN_DAYS for a daily refresh)")
    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
                        help="re-fetch pages even if they already exist")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # In CI, stdout is a pipe (not a TTY), so Python fully buffers it and none
    # of the progress below appears until the process exits — a multi-minute
    # crawl looks frozen. Force line buffering so each line is flushed as it is
    # printed. (`python -u` or PYTHONUNBUFFERED would also work; doing it here
    # keeps the script self-contained regardless of how it is launched.)
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        try:
            stream.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)
        except (AttributeError, ValueError):
            pass

    if args.min_delay > args.max_delay:
        parser.error("--min-delay must not exceed --max-delay")

    out_dir: Path = args.out_dir
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    print(f"[{elapsed()}] Authenticating...")
    token = get_token(args.username, args.password)

    # Reference data: genres (for mapping) and venues (for addresses). Small,
    # so always refresh them alongside the events.
    print(f"[{elapsed()}] Fetching genres and venues...")
    genres = fetch_genres(token)
    (out_dir / "genres_raw.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(genres, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    venues = fetch_venues(token)
    (out_dir / "venues_raw.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(venues, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    print(f"[{elapsed()}]   {len(genres)} genres, {venues.get('total', '?')} venues")

    # First page tells us the total so we know how many pages to fetch.
    print(f"[{elapsed()}] Fetching page 1 (recentlyAdded={args.recently_added}) "
          "to determine total...")
    first = fetch_events_page(token, 1, args.per, args.seed, args.recently_added)
    total = first["total"]
    total_pages = max(1, math.ceil(total / args.per))
    if args.max_pages:
        total_pages = min(total_pages, args.max_pages)
    width = max(2, len(str(total_pages)))
    # Rough finish estimate from the average inter-request delay (each page but
    # the last is followed by one sleep).
    est_secs = (total_pages - 1) * (args.min_delay + args.max_delay) / 2
    print(f"[{elapsed()}] {total} shows across {total_pages} pages (per={args.per}); "
          f"~{int(est_secs // 60)}m of throttled fetching to go")

    all_shows: list[dict] = []

    def save_page(page: int, events: dict) -> None:
        dest = out_dir / f"page_{page:0{width}d}.json"
        tmp = dest.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(events, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
        tmp.replace(dest)

    fetched = skipped = failed = 0
    for page in range(1, total_pages + 1):
        dest = out_dir / f"page_{page:0{width}d}.json"
        if dest.exists() and not args.force:
            try:
                events = json.loads(dest.read_text())
                all_shows.extend(events.get("results", []))
                print(f"[{elapsed()}] [{page}/{total_pages}] skip (exists): "
                      f"{dest.name} ({len(all_shows)} shows so far)")
                skipped += 1
                continue
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
                pass  # fall through and re-fetch a corrupt file

        if page == 1:
            events = first
        else:
            print(f"[{elapsed()}] [{page}/{total_pages}] EventsSearch page={page}")
            try:
                events = fetch_events_page(token, page, args.per, args.seed,
                                           args.recently_added)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — one bad page must not kill the whole crawl; the error is reported and counted in `failed`
                print(f"[{elapsed()}]     ERROR: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
                failed += 1
                continue

        results = events.get("results", [])
        save_page(page, events)
        all_shows.extend(results)
        print(f"[{elapsed()}]     saved {len(results)} shows -> {dest.name} "
              f"({len(all_shows)} total, {fetched + 1}/{total_pages - skipped} fetched)")
        fetched += 1

        if page < total_pages:
            delay = random.uniform(args.min_delay, args.max_delay)
            print(f"[{elapsed()}]     sleeping {delay:.1f}s before next page")
            time.sleep(delay)

    # Flatten everything into one file for convenience.
    shows_path = out_dir / "shows.json"
    shows_path.write_text(json.dumps(all_shows, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    print(f"\n[{elapsed()}] Done. fetched={fetched} skipped={skipped} failed={failed}")
    print(f"[{elapsed()}] Total shows collected: {len(all_shows)} -> {shows_path}")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Normalize scraped edfringe show data into website-ready JSON.
3	
4	Reads the raw scrape (events + venues + genres produced by fetch_shows.py) and
5	emits three layers of data:
6	
7	  data/normalized/shows.json   master, normalized, one record per show with all
8	                               its performances. The source of truth for later
9	                               processing / regenerating the day files. NOT sent
10	                               to the browser.
11	
12	  data/normalized/shows.min.json
13	                               the compact wire form of the master, and the file
14	                               the planner actually downloads. Losslessly packed
15	                               against the venues.json lookups: every enum (genre,
16	                               room, subgenre, ticket status, age restriction) is
17	                               an index into a shared list; venueName is rebuilt
18	                               from the venue code + room; smallImage is dropped
19	                               when it equals image; booleans are 1/0; dates are an
20	                               MMDD int; field names are 1-3 chars. The planner
21	                               rehydrates it with venues.json (see plan/plan.js).
22	
23	  data/normalized/descriptions.min.json
24	                               slug -> full show description, as a sidecar the
25	                               planner fetches SEPARATELY and lazily. It exists
26	                               so the catalogue above stays small enough to block
27	                               on: descriptions are the bulkiest field and are
28	                               needed by nothing on first paint — only by the
29	                               hover card and by search, both of which work
30	                               (from the 160-char `blurb` in the catalogue) and
31	                               simply reach further once this lands.
32	
33	  data/venues.json             shared lookup, sent once:
34	                               {venues, rooms, genres, subgenres, ticketStatuses,
35	                               ageRestrictions}. `venues` is keyed by venue code
36	                               ("venue number") -> name, address, postcode, lat,
37	                               lng; the rest are the global de-duplicated string
38	                               lists the day files and shows.min.json index into.
39	
40	  data/days/2026-08-DD.json    one file per August day, holding only the shows
41	                               performing that day with the minimum a card needs.
42	                               Normalized: venue is referenced by code and
43	                               genre/room by index into the global rooms/genres
44	                               lists (all in venues.json). This is what the site
45	                               loads on open.
46	  data/days/index.json         list of available days + per-day counts.
47	
48	Locations are normalized to a venue code plus the specific room (space) of the
49	show. Price is reduced to a free/paid flag (the listing API exposes no amount).
50	Venue coordinates are geocoded from UK postcodes via postcodes.io and cached in
51	venues.json so a refresh only geocodes new venues.
52	
53	Usage:
54	    python3 scraper/normalize.py                     # full rebuild from raw scrape
55	    python3 scraper/normalize.py --merge             # upsert raw into existing master
56	    python3 scraper/normalize.py --no-geocode        # skip postcode lookups
57	    python3 scraper/normalize.py --minify-from-master  # rebuild venues.json + the
58	                                                     # compact shows.min.json from the
59	                                                     # existing master (no raw scrape)
60	    python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest          # run the built-in fixture test
61	"""
62	
63	from __future__ import annotations
64	
65	import argparse
66	import json
67	import re
68	import sys
69	from pathlib import Path
70	from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
71	from urllib.error import URLError, HTTPError
72	
73	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
74	DEFAULT_RAW_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "raw_pages"
75	DEFAULT_MASTER = ROOT / "data" / "normalized" / "shows.json"
76	DEFAULT_MASTER_MIN = ROOT / "data" / "normalized" / "shows.min.json"
77	DEFAULT_DESCRIPTIONS = ROOT / "data" / "normalized" / "descriptions.min.json"
78	DEFAULT_VENUES = ROOT / "data" / "venues.json"
79	DEFAULT_DAYS_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "days"
80	
81	AUGUST_PREFIX = "2026-08"
82	BLURB_MAX = 160
83	
84	POSTCODES_IO_BULK = "https://api.postcodes.io/postcodes"
85	
86	# Manual coordinate overrides for venues whose postcode the open geocoder can't
87	# resolve (large-user postcodes, park/marquee sites, etc.). Applied last, so
88	# they always win and survive a refresh. code -> (lat, lng).
89	MANUAL_COORDS = {
90	    "360": (55.940946, -3.190175),   # Underbelly's Circus Hub on the Meadows
91	    "147": (55.948692, -3.191961),   # National Library of Scotland
92	    "320": (55.977521, -3.169072),   # Brown's of Leith
93	    "560": (55.946273, -3.206378),   # Scott Lawrie Gallery
94	}
95	
96	# The site's ten official genre categories (must match js/app.js GENRES).
97	SITE_GENRES = [
98	    "Cabaret and Variety",
99	    "Children's Shows",
100	    "Comedy",
101	    "Dance, Physical Theatre & Circus",
102	    "Events",
103	    "Exhibitions",
104	    "Music",
105	    "Musicals and Opera",
106	    "Spoken Word",
107	    "Theatre",
108	]
109	
110	
111	def map_genre(value: str | None, label: str | None) -> str:
112	    """Map an API genre (enum value + human label) to a site category."""
113	    text = f"{value or ''} {label or ''}".lower().replace("&", "and")
114	    # Order matters: check the more specific categories first.
115	    if "cabaret" in text or "variety" in text:
116	        return "Cabaret and Variety"
117	    if "child" in text or "kid" in text:
118	        return "Children's Shows"
119	    if "comedy" in text:
120	        return "Comedy"
121	    if "dance" in text or "physical" in text or "circus" in text:
122	        return "Dance, Physical Theatre & Circus"
123	    if "musical" in text or "opera" in text:
124	        return "Musicals and Opera"
125	    if "music" in text:
126	        return "Music"
127	    if "spoken" in text or "word" in text:
128	        return "Spoken Word"
129	    if "exhibition" in text:
130	        return "Exhibitions"
131	    if "theatre" in text or "theater" in text:
132	        return "Theatre"
133	    if "event" in text:
134	        return "Events"
135	    # Fall back to the label as-is so nothing is silently dropped.
136	    return (label or value or "Events").strip()
137	
138	
139	def subgenre_labels(event: dict) -> list[str]:
140	    """A show's subgenres as display labels (e.g. ["Stand-up", "Improv"]).
141	
142	    The API gives both `subGenre` (a comma-joined human string) and `subgenres`
143	    (the enum list). Prefer the human string — it carries the festival's own
144	    casing ("Sci-Fi", "LGBTQ+", "Artist(s) of colour") that title-casing the
145	    enum can't reproduce — and fall back to humanising the enum. About 2% of
146	    shows carry no subgenre, so the list may be empty.
147	    """
148	    raw = event.get("subGenre")
149	    if raw:
150	        labels = [s.strip() for s in raw.split(",")]
151	    else:
152	        labels = [v.replace("_", " ").title() for v in event.get("subgenres") or []]
153	    seen: set[str] = set()
154	    out: list[str] = []
155	    for label in labels:
156	        key = label.lower()
157	        if label and key not in seen:
158	            seen.add(key)
159	            out.append(label)
160	    return out
161	
162	
163	def clean_description(description: str | None) -> str:
164	    """The full description as plain text: markdown markers dropped, whitespace
165	    collapsed, nothing truncated. This is what the descriptions sidecar carries;
166	    short_blurb() below is the same text cut to a single line for the catalogue."""
167	    if not description:
168	        return ""
169	    text = re.sub(r"[*_#>`]", "", description)        # drop markdown markers
170	    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
171	
172	
173	def short_blurb(description: str | None) -> str:
174	    """A compact one-line blurb: strip markdown, collapse space, truncate."""
175	    text = clean_description(description)
176	    if not text:
177	        return ""
178	    if len(text) <= BLURB_MAX:
179	        return text
180	    cut = text[:BLURB_MAX].rsplit(" ", 1)[0].rstrip(",.;:")
181	    return cut + "…"
182	
183	
184	# Every listing image is served from this single host. The master stores only
185	# the trailing GUID and the client re-attaches the prefix, which trims ~50 bytes

191	    """The client-facing image reference: just the GUID for the known host.

193	    Anything not served from the edfringe image host is kept as a full url, so
194	    an unexpected source still renders (the client treats a value that carries a
195	    scheme as an absolute url).
196	    """
197	    if not url:
198	        return None
199	    if url.startswith(IMAGE_URL_PREFIX):
200	        return url[len(IMAGE_URL_PREFIX):]
201	    return url

233	def is_free(event: dict) -> bool:
234	    if event.get("freeTicketed"):
235	        return True
236	    pt = event.get("priceType")
237	    if not pt:
238	        return False
239	    # priceType may be a string, or a list of strings/objects. Treat the show
240	    # as free only when every price type it offers is a free one.
241	    items = pt if isinstance(pt, list) else [pt]
242	    texts = [json.dumps(x).upper() for x in items]
243	    return bool(texts) and all("FREE" in t for t in texts)

246	def normalize_event(event: dict) -> dict:
247	    """Reduce one raw API event to the master normalized record."""
248	    spaces = event.get("spaces") or []
249	    space = spaces[0] if spaces else {}
250	    venues = event.get("venues") or []
251	
252	    venue_code = space.get("venueCode")
253	    venue_name = space.get("venueName") or (venues[0].get("title") if venues else None)
254	    room = space.get("title")
255	
256	    duration = event.get("duration")
257	    try:
258	        duration = int(duration) if duration not in (None, "") else None
259	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
260	        duration = None
261	
262	    performances = []
263	    for p in event.get("performances") or []:
264	        dt = p.get("dateTime")
265	        if not dt or p.get("cancelled"):
266	            continue
267	        # The API stores Edinburgh wall-clock time; take date/time literally.
268	        performances.append({
269	            "date": dt[:10],
270	            "start": dt[11:16],
271	            "soldOut": bool(p.get("soldOut")),
272	            "status": p.get("ticketStatus") or p.get("status"),
273	        })
274	    performances.sort(key=lambda x: (x["date"], x["start"]))
275	
276	    return {
277	        "id": event.get("cmsRef") or str(event.get("id")),
278	        "title": event.get("title"),
279	        "slug": event.get("slug"),
280	        "genre": map_genre(event.get("genre"), event.get("genre")),

282	        "company": event.get("presentedBy") or None,
283	        "duration": duration,
284	        "ageRestriction": event.get("ageRestriction") or None,

290	        # catalogue (minify_master) and shipped separately, see the descriptions
291	        # sidecar in write_derived_outputs.

293	        "venue": venue_code,

300	def build_venues(venues_raw: dict, existing: dict, geocode: bool) -> dict:
301	    """venue code -> {name, address, postcode, lat, lng}, geocoding new ones."""
302	    results = (venues_raw or {}).get("results") or []
303	    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
304	    to_geocode: dict[str, str] = {}   # postcode -> first venue code needing it
305	
306	    for v in results:
307	        code = v.get("venueCode")
308	        if not code:
309	            continue
310	        addr = ", ".join(p for p in (v.get("address1"), v.get("address2")) if p)
311	        postcode = (v.get("postCode") or "").strip()
312	        prev = existing.get(code, {})
313	        rec = {
314	            "name": v.get("title"),
315	            "address": addr,
316	            "postcode": postcode,
317	            "lat": None,
318	            "lng": None,
319	        }
320	        # Reuse cached coordinates when the postcode is unchanged.
321	        if prev.get("lat") is not None and prev.get("postcode") == postcode:
322	            rec["lat"], rec["lng"] = prev["lat"], prev["lng"]
323	        elif postcode:
324	            to_geocode.setdefault(postcode, code)
325	        out[code] = rec
326	
327	    if geocode and to_geocode:
328	        coords = geocode_postcodes(list(to_geocode.keys()))
329	        for code, rec in out.items():
330	            if rec["lat"] is None and rec["postcode"] in coords:
331	                rec["lat"], rec["lng"] = coords[rec["postcode"]]
332	        hits = sum(1 for r in out.values() if r["lat"] is not None)
333	        print(f"  geocoded {len(coords)} new postcodes; {hits}/{len(out)} venues located")
334	
335	    # Manual overrides win over (and backfill) whatever geocoding produced.
336	    for code, (lat, lng) in MANUAL_COORDS.items():
337	        if code in out:
338	            out[code]["lat"], out[code]["lng"] = lat, lng
339	    return out

342	def geocode_postcodes(postcodes: list[str]) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]:
343	    """Bulk-geocode UK postcodes via postcodes.io. Best-effort: returns what it can."""
344	    coords: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
345	    for i in range(0, len(postcodes), 100):
346	        chunk = postcodes[i:i + 100]
347	        body = json.dumps({"postcodes": chunk}).encode("utf-8")
348	        req = Request(POSTCODES_IO_BULK, data=body,
349	                      headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
350	        try:
351	            with urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
352	                data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
353	        except (URLError, HTTPError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
354	            print(f"  WARNING: geocoding failed for a chunk: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
355	            continue
356	        for item in data.get("result", []):
357	            res = item.get("result")
358	            if res and res.get("latitude") is not None:
359	                coords[item["query"]] = (round(res["latitude"], 6),
360	                                         round(res["longitude"], 6))
361	    return coords

364	def unify_subgenre_casing(master: list[dict]) -> None:
365	    """Collapse case-variant subgenres to one display casing, in place.
366	
367	    The festival's free-text `subGenre` is inconsistently cased across shows, so
368	    the same tag arrives as both "Alternative Comedy" and "Alternative comedy" —
369	    which would otherwise show as two distinct tags. For each case-folded
370	    subgenre, pick the most title-cased variant (the festival's own labels are
371	    Title Case; the lowercase forms are data-entry slips, even when commoner),
372	    breaking ties by frequency then alphabetically. Deterministic across runs,
373	    and it keeps the nicer form ("LGBTQ+", "Sci-Fi", "Artist(s) of Colour").
374	    """
375	    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
376	    variants: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
377	    for show in master:
378	        for label in show.get("subgenres") or []:
379	            counts[label] = counts.get(label, 0) + 1
380	            variants.setdefault(label.casefold(), set()).add(label)
381	
382	    def rank(v: str) -> tuple:
383	        titleish = sum(1 for w in v.split() if w[:1].isupper())
384	        return (-titleish, -counts[v], v)
385	
386	    canon = {key: sorted(vs, key=rank)[0] for key, vs in variants.items()}
387	    for show in master:
388	        seen: set[str] = set()
389	        out: list[str] = []
390	        for label in show.get("subgenres") or []:
391	            picked = canon.get(label.casefold(), label)
392	            if picked.casefold() not in seen:
393	                seen.add(picked.casefold())
394	                out.append(picked)
395	        show["subgenres"] = out
396

398	def build_lookups(master: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
399	    """The global (genres, rooms, subgenres, ticketStatuses, ageRestrictions)
400	    lookup lists: every distinct genre, room, subgenre, per-performance ticket
401	    status and age restriction across all shows, sorted. A show references them by
402	    index in the day files and in shows.min.json; the lists ship once, alongside
403	    the venues (run())."""
404	    genres = sorted({s["genre"] for s in master if s.get("genre")})
405	    rooms = sorted({s["room"] for s in master if s.get("room")})
406	    subgenres = sorted({sg for s in master for sg in s.get("subgenres") or []})
407	    ticket_statuses = sorted({p.get("status") for s in master
408	                              for p in s.get("performances") or [] if p.get("status")})
409	    age_restrictions = sorted({s["ageRestriction"] for s in master if s.get("ageRestriction")})
410	    return genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses, age_restrictions

413	def build_day_files(master: list[dict], genre_ix: dict[str, int],
414	                    room_ix: dict[str, int], sub_ix: dict[str, int],
415	                    ts_ix: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, list]:
416	    """Bucket shows by August performance date into minimal per-day records.
417	
418	    Each record is kept small:
419	
420	      * `genre` / `room` — pointers into the global `genres` / `rooms` lookup
421	        lists (shipped once with the venues), not the strings themselves.
422	        `room` is -1 when the show has no specific room.
423	      * `subs` — the show's subgenres as pointers into the global `subgenres`
424	        lookup list; an empty list when the festival tagged none (~2%).
425	      * `ts` — this performance's ticket status as a pointer into the global
426	        `ticketStatuses` lookup (-1 if unknown). This is the reliable "can I get
427	        a ticket" signal; the `soldOut` flag is not (a show can be soldOut:false
428	        yet have no online allocation).
429	      * `free` / `soldOut` — 1/0 rather than true/false.
430	      * `blurb` — omitted. It is kept in the master (the scraped data) but the
431	        site never renders it, so it is left out of the per-day payload.
432	    """
433	    days: dict[str, list] = {}
434	    seen: set[tuple] = set()   # (id, date, start) — drop duplicate performances
435	    for show in master:
436	        for p in show.get("performances", []):
437	            date = p["date"]
438	            if not date.startswith(AUGUST_PREFIX):
439	                continue
440	            key = (show["id"], date, p["start"])
441	            if key in seen:
442	                continue
443	            seen.add(key)
444	            days.setdefault(date, []).append({
445	                "id": show["id"],
446	                "title": show["title"],
447	                "genre": genre_ix.get(show.get("genre"), -1),
448	                "subs": [sub_ix[sg] for sg in show.get("subgenres") or []
449	                         if sg in sub_ix],
450	                "venue": show["venue"],
451	                "room": room_ix.get(show.get("room"), -1),
452	                "start": p["start"],
453	                "duration": show["duration"],
454	                "free": 1 if show["free"] else 0,
455	                "soldOut": 1 if p["soldOut"] else 0,
456	                "ts": ts_ix.get(p.get("status"), -1),
457	                "slug": show["slug"],
458	            })
459	    for date in days:
460	        days[date].sort(key=lambda x: (x["start"], x["title"] or ""))
461	    return days

465	# Compact wire form of the master (data/normalized/shows.min.json).
466	#
467	# The planner downloads this, not the 7 MB master. It is packed against the same
468	# venues.json lookups the day files use, so it carries no dictionaries of its own,
469	# and the packing is lossless — plan/plan.js rebuilds the full records from it.

472	def month_day_key(date: str) -> int:
473	    """A 2026 date as an MMDD integer: "2026-08-07" -> 807, "2026-07-24" -> 724.
474	
475	    Every performance is in 2026 (the festival year), so the year is implied and
476	    only the month/day need storing; the client re-attaches "2026-".
477	    """
478	    return int(date[5:7] + date[8:10])

481	def venue_name_rebuildable(show: dict, venues: dict) -> bool:
482	    """True when a show's venueName is exactly "<room> at <venue name>" (or the
483	    bare venue name when it has no room), so it can be dropped from the wire form
484	    and rebuilt client-side from the venue code + room. False for the handful of
485	    shows with no resolvable venue (or any venueName that wouldn't rebuild
486	    byte-for-byte) — those keep their venueName verbatim, so packing stays
487	    lossless whatever the data does."""
488	    code = show.get("venue")
489	    if not code or code not in venues:
490	        return False
491	    name = venues[code].get("name")
492	    room = show.get("room")
493	    rebuilt = f"{room} at {name}" if room else name
494	    return rebuilt == show.get("venueName")

497	def minify_master(master: list[dict], genre_ix: dict[str, int], room_ix: dict[str, int],
498	                  sub_ix: dict[str, int], ts_ix: dict[str, int], age_ix: dict[str, int],
499	                  venues: dict) -> list[dict]:
500	    """Pack the full master into the compact records the planner downloads.
501	
502	    Each field is either shortened, indexed into a shared venues.json lookup, or
503	    dropped when it can be reconstructed:
504	
505	      * `g`/`rm`/`ar` — genre, room and age restriction as indices into the
506	        global genres/rooms/ageRestrictions lists (-1 when absent).
507	      * `sg` — subgenres as indices into the global subgenres list.
508	      * `p[].t` — the performance ticket status as an index into ticketStatuses
509	        (-1 when absent).
510	      * `vn` — venueName, kept ONLY when it can't be rebuilt from `v` + `rm`
511	        (venue_name_rebuildable); present-but-null for the no-venue shows.
512	      * `si` — smallImage, kept ONLY when it differs from `im` (image); otherwise
513	        the client mirrors image.
514	      * `f`/`p[].o` — free / soldOut as 1/0.
515	      * `p[].d` — the performance date as an MMDD int.
516	      * `im` — the bare image GUID; the client re-attaches the host prefix.
517	    """
518	    out: list[dict] = []
519	    for s in master:
520	        rec: dict = {
521	            "i": s["id"],
522	            "t": s["title"],
523	            "sl": s["slug"],
524	            "g": genre_ix.get(s.get("genre"), -1),
525	            "sg": [sub_ix[sg] for sg in s.get("subgenres") or [] if sg in sub_ix],
526	            "c": s.get("company"),
527	            "d": s.get("duration"),
528	            "ar": age_ix.get(s.get("ageRestriction"), -1),
529	            "f": 1 if s.get("free") else 0,
530	            "im": s.get("image"),
531	        }
532	        if s.get("smallImage") != s.get("image"):
533	            rec["si"] = s.get("smallImage")
534	        rec["b"] = s.get("blurb") or ""
535	        rec["v"] = s.get("venue")
536	        if not venue_name_rebuildable(s, venues):
537	            rec["vn"] = s.get("venueName")
538	        rec["rm"] = room_ix.get(s.get("room"), -1)
539	        rec["p"] = [{
540	            "d": month_day_key(p["date"]),
541	            "s": p["start"],
542	            "o": 1 if p["soldOut"] else 0,
543	            "t": ts_ix.get(p.get("status"), -1),
544	        } for p in s.get("performances") or []]
545	        out.append(rec)
546	    return out

549	def build_descriptions(master: list[dict]) -> dict:
550	    """The descriptions sidecar: {"v": 1, "d": {slug: text}}.
551	
552	    Falls back to a show's `blurb` when it has no `description` — masters
553	    scraped before descriptions were retained carry only the truncated blurb,
554	    and half a sentence is still better for search than nothing. Shows with
555	    neither are omitted entirely rather than mapped to "", which keeps the file
556	    to what it is actually for.
557	
558	    Not packed against venues.json like the other wire files: it is keyed by
559	    slug and indexes into nothing, so it can be regenerated, cached and expired
560	    on its own schedule without touching the lookup lists.
561	    """
562	    out: dict[str, str] = {}
563	    for show in master:
564	        slug = show.get("slug")
565	        text = show.get("description") or show.get("blurb") or ""
566	        if slug and text:
567	            out[slug] = text
568	    return {"v": 1, "d": out}

588	def write_derived_outputs(master: list[dict], venues: dict, venues_path: Path,
589	                          days_dir: Path, master_min_path: Path,
590	                          descriptions_path: Path) -> int:
591	    """Write everything derived from the master + venue map: the shared lookup
592	    file (venues.json), the per-day now-page files, the compact planner file
593	    (shows.min.json) and its descriptions sidecar. Returns the number of day
594	    files written.
595	
596	    The lookup lists are built once here and indexed into by both the day files
597	    and shows.min.json, so the two stay in lockstep with a single source of truth.
598	    """
599	    genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses, age_restrictions = build_lookups(master)
600	    write_json(venues_path, {"venues": venues, "rooms": rooms, "genres": genres,
601	                             "subgenres": subgenres, "ticketStatuses": ticket_statuses,
602	                             "ageRestrictions": age_restrictions})
603	
604	    genre_ix = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(genres)}
605	    room_ix = {r: i for i, r in enumerate(rooms)}
606	    sub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subgenres)}
607	    ts_ix = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(ticket_statuses)}
608	    age_ix = {a: i for i, a in enumerate(age_restrictions)}
609	
610	    # Compact planner payload (packed against the lookups just written), and the
611	    # descriptions it deliberately leaves behind.
612	    write_json(master_min_path, minify_master(master, genre_ix, room_ix, sub_ix,
613	                                              ts_ix, age_ix, venues))
614	    write_json(descriptions_path, build_descriptions(master))
615	
616	    # Per-day August files + index.
617	    days = build_day_files(master, genre_ix, room_ix, sub_ix, ts_ix)
618	    for date, items in days.items():
619	        write_json(days_dir / f"{date}.json", items)
620	    write_json(days_dir / "index.json", {
621	        "dates": sorted(days.keys()),
622	        "counts": {d: len(days[d]) for d in sorted(days)},
623	        "shows": len(master),
624	        "venues": len(venues),
625	    })
626	    return len(days)

629	def regen_from_master(args) -> int:
630	    """Rebuild venues.json + the compact shows.min.json from the committed master,
631	    without a raw scrape. Used to (re)generate the planner payload after a manual
632	    master edit, or to backfill it the first time. The venue map (with its cached
633	    coordinates) is carried over from the existing venues.json verbatim; only the
634	    lookup lists and the derived files are rebuilt from the master."""
635	    master_path = Path(args.master)

637	    venues_path = Path(args.venues)

639	    venues = prior.get("venues", prior)
640	    n_days = write_derived_outputs(master, venues, venues_path,
641	                                   Path(args.days_dir), Path(args.master_min),
642	                                   Path(args.descriptions))
643	    print(f"Regenerated from {master_path} ({len(master)} shows): "
644	          f"{args.master_min}, {args.descriptions}, {venues_path} "
645	          f"({len(venues)} venues), {n_days} day files in {args.days_dir}")
646	    return 0

649	def run(args) -> int:
650	    raw_dir = Path(args.raw_dir)
651	    events = load_events(raw_dir)
652	    print(f"Loaded {len(events)} raw events from {raw_dir}")
653	
654	    normalized = []
655	    skipped = 0
656	    for e in events:
657	        if not e:
658	            continue
659	        try:
660	            normalized.append(normalize_event(e))
661	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - resilience over one bad record
662	            skipped += 1
663	            print(f"  WARNING: skipped event {e.get('id')}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
664	    if skipped:
665	        print(f"  skipped {skipped} unparseable events")
666	
667	    # Master: merge (upsert by id) or replace.
668	    master_path = Path(args.master)
669	    if args.merge and master_path.exists():
670	        by_id = {s["id"]: s for s in json.loads(master_path.read_text())}
671	        for s in normalized:
672	            by_id[s["id"]] = s
673	        master = list(by_id.values())
674	        print(f"Merged {len(normalized)} into master -> {len(master)} shows")
675	    else:
676	        master = normalized
677	        print(f"Master rebuilt with {len(master)} shows")
678	    master.sort(key=lambda s: (s["title"] or "").lower())
679	    unify_subgenre_casing(master)  # one display casing per subgenre across all shows
680	    write_json(master_path, master)
681	
682	    # Global lookup file: the venue map plus the shared rooms/genres lists that
683	    # the day files index into. Sent to the browser once. Venues are always
684	    # rebuilt from the full venue list, coordinates cached. Accepts either the
685	    # bare venue map (old format) or the {venues, ...} container as prior state.
